---
title: "The Dirichlet process mixture, generated"
subtitle: "Catalog P-09 · rung 7 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part II)"
description: "Points arrive one at a time; stick pieces and their means are created only when needed. Points, components and clusters grow at three different speeds."
toc: false
---

The Dirichlet process mixture puts the pieces together. Each new point draws a uniform u.
If u falls inside a piece of the stick that already exists, the point joins that piece's
cluster. If it falls in the unbroken rest, the stick is broken further, one Beta(1, alpha)
proportion at a time, until a piece covers u; every new piece also gets a new mean, drawn
from the base distribution N(0, sigma0^2). The point then lands near its piece's mean, with
spread sigma.

## What to try

- **Add 1** (or Enter) a few times, then **Add 100**. Three counters move at different
  speeds: N grows by one per point, components by one per new piece of stick, clusters by
  one per piece that receives its first point. Clusters grow roughly like alpha log N (the
  dashed curve).
- **Look for lonely black squares.** A u that lands far to the right forces several breaks
  at once; the pieces it skipped get means but no points. Those are components without a
  cluster.
- **Hover over a piece** of the stick (or use the component picker) to light up its points
  and its mean.
- **alpha, sigma0, sigma.** alpha sets how quickly new pieces are needed; sigma0 how far
  apart the means are; sigma how tight each cluster is.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
On this site K_J counts clusters, the fitted components among the J units, not the components
the process has created. After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part II, demo 6); the mathematics is
re-implemented and no code is copied.
:::
